title: Medicare Part A vs Part B: What Is Actually Free and What Costs Money
bigPicture: Part A often has no monthly bill, but both parts have out-of-pocket costs you must pay.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Part A covers hospital stays. Most people pay no monthly premium if they worked and paid Medicare taxes for 10 years.
Part B covers doctor visits and outpatient care. You pay a monthly premium plus a yearly deductible.
Neither part is free. You pay deductibles, copays, and coinsurance for services.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming Part A is free because there is no premium. You still pay hospital deductibles and coinsurance.
Delaying Part B enrollment without other coverage. You will pay a lifelong late penalty.
actionSteps: Check your Social Security statement to confirm Part A premium status.
Sign up for Part B during your Initial Enrollment Period at age 65 unless you have other coverage.
Set aside money for the Part B premium and Part A hospital deductible each year.
